findings.title: Salesforce getClient always refreshes tokens unconditionally and bypasses credential sync
Google refresh stores a SafeParseReturnType instead of the key
Sync-endpoint Response is not unwrapped for non-fetch callers
Placeholder refresh_token is written and the minimum schema is malformed
Webhook secret comparison is not constant-time and fails open when unset
Unhandled parse and decrypt errors in the webhook
Office365 error logging removed and failure silently ignored

response:
## 1) Severity: CRITICAL | Type: Bug
Title: Salesforce getClient always refreshes tokens unconditionally and bypasses credential sync

Affected:
- packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75-99

Explanation:
A token refresh fetch is added on every connection creation, with no expiry check and no use of refreshOAuthTokens. This adds a network call to every operation and breaks the sync path. It also checks `response.statusText !== "OK"`, which is fragile (HTTP/2 has no status text). The parsed result's `success` is used, but `parseRefreshTokenResponse` can throw instead. With sync enabled, the minimal schema is used and the stored key lacks the real refresh token and other fields. Use refreshOAuthTokens, check `response.ok`, and refresh only when needed.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
const response = await refreshOAuthTokens(() => fetch(...), "salesforce", credential.userId);
if (!response.ok) throw new HttpError({ statusCode: 400, message: response.statusText });
~~~

## 2) Severity: CRITICAL | Type: Bug
Title: Google refresh stores a SafeParseReturnType instead of the key

Affected:
- packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:86-100

Explanation:
`parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a safeParse result object `{success, data}`, but it is saved directly as `key`. This corrupts the stored credential. In addition, `res` from refreshOAuthTokens in sync mode is a fetch Response, so `res?.data` is undefined and `token.access_token` throws. The same happens in the other call sites: the Zoom `parsedToken` use and the Office365 handling are inconsistent with the returned shape. Use `.data` and parse the JSON body of the sync response.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
const parsed = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);
const key = parsed.data;
~~~

## 3) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug
Title: Sync-endpoint Response is not unwrapped for non-fetch callers

Affected:
- packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-15
- packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177-189
- packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts:204-217
- packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:85-94

Explanation:
The sync path returns a raw fetch Response. Callers that expect an axios response (`.data`) or a hubspot token object get a Response, so they break. Also the fetch result is never checked for `ok`, and no auth/secret is sent to the endpoint. Normalize the return shape per caller.

## 4) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug
Title: Wrong userId passed in zoho-bigin

Affected:
- packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:93

Explanation:
`credentialId` is passed where a userId is expected, so the sync endpoint is asked about the wrong user.

## 5) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug
Title: Placeholder refresh_token is written and the minimum schema is malformed

Affected:
- packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5-27

Explanation:
`[z.string().toString()]` evaluates to a literal string key, not a wildcard, so the schema requires a property with a weird name and fails validation, or does not behave as the comment says. Also, the literal "refresh_token" is injected as a real refresh token even in non-sync mode, overwriting or masking a missing token. Use `.passthrough()` with an explicit expiry field, and only default the refresh token in sync mode.

## 6) Severity: HIGH | Type: Security
Title: Webhook secret comparison is not constant-time and fails open when unset

Affected:
- apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-29

Explanation:
A plain `!==` comparison is vulnerable to timing attacks. The header may be an array. Use `timingSafeEqual` on strings.

## 7) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Unhandled parse and decrypt errors in the webhook

Affected:
- apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31-59

Explanation:
`parse` and `JSON.parse`/decrypt throw, returning 500 with stack info instead of 400. Also no HTTP method check. Use `safeParse` and a try/catch.

## 8) Severity: LOW | Type: Bug
Title: Zoho Bigin redirect URI hard-coded

Affected:
- packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/api/add.ts:17

Explanation:
This is an unrelated change that duplicates the slug and can drift from the config.

## 9) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Office365 error logging removed and failure silently ignored

Affected:
- packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:263-264

Explanation:
The parse helper now throws on failure, so the `tokenResponse.success &&` check is dead code. The diagnostic logging was dropped, and a failed refresh now throws where it previously proceeded.
